Package com.datastax.oss.driver.api.mapper

Class MapperBuilder<MapperT>

  • java.lang.Object
    • com.datastax.oss.driver.api.mapper.MapperBuilder<MapperT>
  • public abstract class MapperBuilder<MapperT>
extends Object
    Builds an instance of a Mapper-annotated interface wrapping a CqlSession.

    The mapper generates an implementation of this class for every such interface. It is either named <InterfaceName>Builder, or what you provided in Mapper.builderName().

      • withDefaultKeyspace

        @NonNull
public MapperBuilder<MapperT> withDefaultKeyspace​(@Nullable
                                                  com.datastax.oss.driver.api.core.CqlIdentifier keyspaceId)
        Specifies a default keyspace that will be used for all DAOs built with this mapper (unless they specify their own keyspace).

        In other words, given the following definitions: 

         @Mapper
 public interface InventoryMapper {
   @DaoFactory
   ProductDao productDao();

   @DaoFactory
   ProductDao productDao(@DaoKeyspace CqlIdentifier keyspace);
 }

 InventoryMapper mapper1 = new InventoryMapperBuilder(session)
     .withDefaultKeyspace(CqlIdentifier.fromCql("ks1"))
     .build();
 InventoryMapper mapper2 = new InventoryMapperBuilder(session)
     .withDefaultKeyspace(CqlIdentifier.fromCql("ks2"))
     .build();
        Then:
        • mapper1.productDao() will use keyspace ks1;
        • mapper2.productDao() will use keyspace ks2;
        • mapper1.productDao(CqlIdentifier.fromCql("ks3")) will use keyspace ks3.
        See Also:
        DaoFactory

      • withDefaultExecutionProfileName

        @NonNull
public MapperBuilder<MapperT> withDefaultExecutionProfileName​(@Nullable
                                                              String executionProfileName)
        Specifies a default execution profile name that will be used for all DAOs built with this mapper (unless they specify their own execution profile).

        This works the same way as the default keyspace.

        Note that if you had already set a profile with #withDefaultExecutionProfile, this method erases it.

        See Also:

        Specifies a default execution profile name that will be used for all DAOs built with this mapper (unless they specify their own execution profile).

        This works the same way as the default keyspace.

        Note that if you had already set a profile name with #withDefaultExecutionProfileName, this method erases it.

      • withSchemaValidationEnabled

        public MapperBuilder<MapperT> withSchemaValidationEnabled​(boolean enableSchemaValidation)
        Whether to validate mapped entities against the database schema.

        If this is enabled, then every time a new DAO gets created, for each entity referenced in the DAO, the mapper will check that there is a corresponding table or UDT.

        • for each entity field, the database table or UDT must contain a column with the corresponding name (according to the NamingStrategy).
        • the types must be compatible, according to the CodecRegistry used by the session.
        • additionally, if the target element is a table, the primary key must be properly annotated in the entity.
        If any of those steps fails, an IllegalArgumentException is thrown.

        Schema validation is enabled by default; it adds a small startup overhead, so once your application is stable you may want to disable it.

        See Also:
        SchemaHint

      • withCustomState

        @NonNull
public MapperBuilder<MapperT> withCustomState​(@Nullable
                                              Object key,
                                              @Nullable
                                              Object value)
        Stores custom state that will be propagated to MapperContext.getCustomState().

        This is intended mainly for QueryProvider methods: since provider classes are instantiated directly by the generated mapper code, they have no way to access non-static state from the rest of your application. This method allows you to pass that state while building the mapper, and access it later at runtime.

        Note that this state will be accessed concurrently, it should be thread-safe.
